interpretation: Reading B (universal), first half: 'every object of thought (πᾶν τὸ διανοητὸν καὶ νοητὸν), thought either affirms or denies' is read as a claim about every object of thought: whatever is the object of some thought is affirmed or denied (STMT-OBJECT-OF-THOUGHT-AFFIRMED-OR-DENIED). The extension to every proposition, STMT-THOUGHT-AFFIRMS-OR-DENIES-EVERY-PROPOSITION, is not attributed to this sentence: it is the formalization's own open premise.
